blocks.content: Rotation is Earth's spinning movement on its axis from west to east. Because of this direction, the Sun appears to move east to west.

cells: 23h 56m — time taken relative to distant stars.
24h — time taken for the Sun to reappear at the same position.

blocks.content: Rotation is Earth's spinning movement on its axis from west to east.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Rotation is defined as Earth spinning on its axis from west to east.
Because Earth rotates from west to east, the Sun appears to move from east to west across the sky.
The solar day is longer than the sidereal day because Earth must rotate slightly more than 360° to realign with the Sun while advancing in its orbit.
Major impacts of rotation include day and night, time zone formation, daily temperature fluctuations, equatorial bulge, and the Coriolis effect.

blocks.content: While Earth rotates, it also moves along its orbit. Therefore, it must rotate slightly more than 360° for the Sun to appear in the same position — making the solar day longer.

rows: Measures single complete spin relative to distant position
Requires extra rotation because Earth also moves along its orbit around the Sun

items: Direction of Rotation vs. Apparent Movement: Earth rotates West to East; consequently, the Sun appears to move East to West.
Sidereal Day vs. Solar Day: The Solar day is longer than the Sidereal day because Earth must rotate slightly more than 360° due to its simultaneous orbital movement.

Direct Effects of Rotation: Questions often ask to identify effects of rotation vs. revolution—remember that the Coriolis effect, equatorial bulge, time zones, and daily temperature variations are caused by rotation.
